'''''Persicaria pensylvanica''''' (syn. ''Polygonum pensylvanicum''<ref name=POWO_695100-1/>) is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[buckwheat]] family, [[Polygonaceae]]. It is native to parts of [[North America]], where it is widespread in Canada and the United States.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 4 January 2018}}</ref> It has also been noted as an [[introduced species]] in parts of Europe and South America.<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250037745 ''Persicaria pensylvanica''.] Flora of North America.</ref> Common names include '''Pennsylvania smartweed''', '''pinkweed''', and '''common smartweed'''.<ref name=grin/>

== Description ==
Pennsylvania smartweed is a variable annual herb reaching {{convert|10|cm|in|abbr=on}} to {{convert|2|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall. The upright, ribbed stems are branching or unbranched. The lance-shaped leaves have a short [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] and a blade about {{cvt|4|-|17|cm|in}} long, sometimes up to {{cvt|23|cm|in|0}}. The blade may be marked with a dark blotch. The brownish  [[ochrea]] at the base is up to {{convert|2|cm|in|abbr=on}}. The [[inflorescences]] grow at the top of the stem and from the leaf axils. The flowers have five pinkish or greenish [[tepal]]s each a few millimeters long.<ref name=fna/>

This plant grows in moist, disturbed habitat types, such as ponds, [[reservoir]]s, riverbanks, irrigated fields, and ditches.<ref name=fna/>

==Ecology==
This plant is an important part of the habitat for [[waterfowl]] and other birds, which use it for food and cover. At least 50 species of birds have been observed feeding on the seeds, including [[duck]]s, [[goose|geese]], [[Rallidae|rails]], [[Colinus|bobwhites]], [[mourning dove]], and [[ring-necked pheasant]]. The seeds and other parts are eaten by mammals such as the [[white-footed mouse]], [[muskrat]], [[raccoon]], and [[fox squirrel]].<ref name=nrcs>[https://plants.usda.gov/factsheet/pdf/fs_pope2.pdf ''Polygonum pensylvanicum'' L.] Plant Fact Sheet. USDA NRCS.</ref>

==Traditional native American medicine==
[[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native Americans]] have various uses for the plant. The [[Ojibwe people|Chippewa]] use it for [[epilepsy]].<ref name=umich>[http://herb.umd.umich.edu/herb/search.pl?searchstring=Polygonum+pensylvanicum ''Polygonum pensylvanicum''] Native American Ethnobotany. University of Michigan, Dearborn.</ref><ref>Gilmore, Melvin R. 1933 Some Chippewa Uses of Plants. Ann Arbor. University of Michigan Press (p. 129)</ref> The [[Iroquois]] use it for [[horse colic]].<ref name=umich/><ref>Herrick, James William 1977 Iroquois Medical Botany. State University of New York, Albany, PhD Thesis (p. 314)</ref> The [[Menominee]] take a leaf infusion for hemorrhage of blood from the mouth and post-partum healing.<ref name=umich/><ref>Smith, Huron H. 1923 Ethnobotany of the Menomini Indians. Bulletin of the Public Museum of the City of Milwaukee 4:1-174 (p. 47)</ref> The [[Meskwaki]] use it on bleeding [[hemorrhoid]]s.<ref name=umich/><ref>Smith, Huron H. 1928 Ethnobotany of the Meskwaki Indians. Bulletin of the Public Museum of the City of Milwaukee 4:175-326 (p. 236,237)</ref>
